description: This is a modern 'Global View' dashboard for your Kubernetes cluster(s). Made for kube-prometheus-stack and take advantage of the latest Grafana features. GitHub repository: https://github.com/dotdc/grafana-dashboards-kubernetes

links.title: Fleet overview
links.tooltip: The home page: is anything wrong, and where?

links.title: Kubernetes views
links.tooltip: Cluster, namespace and pod drill-down views

panels.title: Global CPU  Usage
panels.description: CPU used across all nodes as a share of their cores, from the root cgroup of each node. Sustained above 70% means the cluster is short of CPU: add nodes or trim requests.

panels.title: Global RAM Usage
panels.description: Memory in use (working set) across all nodes as a share of their RAM. Sustained above 80% means eviction risk: add nodes or find the heavy namespace below.

panels.title: Nodes
panels.description: Nodes registered in the cluster. A drop with no planned scale-down is a node lost: check the Nodes NotReady tile on the Fleet overview.

panels.title: Kubernetes Resource Count
panels.description: How many of each Kubernetes object the cluster holds. Use it to spot a runaway controller creating objects without bound.

panels.title: Namespaces
panels.description: Namespaces in the cluster. An unexpected change is a provisioning or cleanup event worth tracing.

panels.title: CPU Usage
panels.description: CPU cores in use across all nodes. Compare with the cores available above to see the headroom.

panels.title: RAM Usage
panels.description: Memory in use (working set) across all nodes, in bytes. Compare with the RAM available to see the headroom.

panels.title: Running Pods
panels.description: Pods in the Running phase. A sudden drop with no deploy means workloads are being evicted or a node was lost.

panels.title: Cluster CPU Utilization
panels.description: Cluster CPU used as a share of all cores, over time. Read the shape: a plateau near the top is saturation, a spike is a burst.

panels.title: Cluster Memory Utilization
panels.description: Cluster memory in use as a share of all RAM, over time. A steady climb is a leak somewhere: find the namespace in the panels below.

panels.title: CPU Utilization by namespace
panels.description: CPU cores used per namespace. The top line is the heaviest tenant of the cluster; click a series to open that namespace.

panels.title: Memory Utilization by namespace
panels.description: Working-set memory per namespace. The top line is the heaviest tenant; a steady climb is a leak. Click a series to open that namespace.

panels.title: CPU Utilization by instance
panels.description: CPU used per node as a share of its cores. One node far above the rest means uneven scheduling: check for a large pod or missing anti-affinity.

panels.title: Memory Utilization by instance
panels.description: Working-set memory per node. One node near its RAM means eviction risk: look at what runs there.
No data is generally a good thing here.
panels.title: CPU Throttled seconds by namespace
Kubernetes Pods QoS classes
panels.description: Pods by quality-of-service class. Many BestEffort pods are the first evicted under pressure: give them requests.

panels.title: Kubernetes Pods Status Reason
panels.description: Pods whose status carries a reason (for example Evicted or NodeLost). Anything here is a pod the cluster gave up on: find the reason and its node.
No data is generally a good thing here.
panels.title: OOM Events by namespace

panels.description: No data is generally a good thing here.
panels.title: Container Restarts by namespace
Network Received by namespace
panels.description: Bytes per second received by pods, per namespace. A sudden rise is a traffic spike or a chatty workload.
